nodes.label: actor-ts framework
nodes.rationale: A batteries-included actor-model runtime for TypeScript running natively on Bun, Node.js and Deno; Apache 2.0, pre-1.0, experimental.

nodes.label: AI-assisted hobby-project disclaimer
nodes.rationale: Coverage is good but the surface area is enormous and none of it is battle-tested; the badge figures are measured on hosted runners where three multi-node suites are skipped, so the README states that rather than letting the number imply more than it proves.

nodes.label: Actors and supervision
nodes.rationale: Single-threaded per-mailbox processing, lifecycle hooks, stash, timers, become/unbecome and supervision (restart / resume / stop / escalate).

nodes.label: Cluster membership and failure detection
nodes.rationale: Gossip membership, phi-accrual failure detection, split-brain resolvers, weakly-up, and multiple transports (TCP, MessageChannel, in-memory).

nodes.label: Cluster sharding
nodes.rationale: The framework routes per-entity messages to the owning node and migrates entities as nodes come and go; ShardKey declares identity on the actor class so neither the type name nor the entity-id extractor is repeated at the call site.

nodes.label: Cluster singleton
nodes.rationale: One node hosts it, the rest hold a forwarding ref, and failover moves it without callers changing anything; start() is get-or-create so calling it from several modules is safe.

nodes.label: Distributed Data (CRDTs)
nodes.rationale: Nine CRDTs (counters, registers, sets, maps) with a durable-storage backend, quorum reads/writes and automatic gossip.

nodes.label: Persistence — event sourcing and durable state
nodes.rationale: PersistentActor, DurableState, snapshots, projections with a per-projection handler-failure strategy, persistence-query and replicated event sourcing, over journals for in-memory, SQLite, libSQL/Turso, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MS SQL, MongoDB, DynamoDB, Cloudflare D1 and Cassandra/ScyllaDB.

nodes.label: Object storage with compression and encryption
nodes.rationale: S3 / MinIO / R2 / filesystem with optional gzip or zstd compression and client-side AES-256-GCM encryption, using per-tenant subkeys derived via HKDF.

nodes.label: HTTP routing DSL and backends
nodes.rationale: Directive-style routing with Fastify by default plus Express and Hono backends, response caching, rate limiting, idempotency-key dedup, a security-middleware suite and backend-agnostic static file serving.

nodes.label: Typed WebSocket routes
nodes.rationale: websocket(path, actorRef) binds a WebsocketServerActor with typed messages, reply/broadcast and connect/disconnect hooks; WebsocketClientActor is the reconnecting client half.

nodes.label: Message-broker integrations
nodes.rationale: A single BrokerActor base with Kafka, MQTT, AMQP, NATS, Redis-Streams, gRPC, SSE, raw TCP/UDP and IMAP/SMTP integrations; reconnect-with-backoff, outbound buffer and subscriber fan-out are baked into the base rather than repeated per adapter.

nodes.label: Pluggable cache
nodes.rationale: One Cache interface over in-memory, Redis and Memcached backends.

nodes.label: Typed options with fail-fast validation
nodes.rationale: One fluent XOptions builder per configurable thing, validated once on the merged settings so a bad port, timeout or URL throws an OptionsError at startup rather than deep in a later code path.

nodes.label: Utility primitives and helpers
nodes.rationale: Option/Try/Either/Lazy, BidirectionalMap and BidirectionalMultiMap that survive a snapshot as real instances with no adapter, plus randomString/randomHex/randomId/randomUuid with an optional exists predicate so 'keep drawing until one is free' is the call itself, safeStringify and lazyImportModule.

nodes.label: Dead letters and the dead-letter queue
nodes.rationale: Every undeliverable message is published on the event stream; opting in to system.deadLetterQueue also keeps them in a bounded ring or a journal-backed one, replayable by id with a replay cap so a poison message cannot be retried into an ever-growing queue.

nodes.label: Observability — metrics, tracing, management endpoints
nodes.rationale: Prometheus exporter, OTel tracing, management HTTP endpoints (/health, /ready, /cluster/members, /sharding/regions) and out-of-the-box stock metrics.

nodes.label: Multi-sink logging
nodes.rationale: One record fans out to several destinations at once, each with its own minimum level, bounded queues, batched delivery and a flush on shutdown; every integration is dependency-free (Sentry is a passthrough to your own SDK) and a transform hook redacts once, before fan-out.

nodes.label: DevTools embedded web UI
nodes.rationale: Reads only by default — sending a message into the system is a separate, off-by-default acknowledgement. Angular and ECharts are build-time only so neither appears in the package's dependencies and the served page loads nothing over the network; loopback-only and unauthenticated by default, and it refuses a routable bind without a gate.

nodes.label: TestKit
nodes.rationale: TestProbe, ManualScheduler and MultiNodeSpec for deterministic tests including cluster scenarios.

nodes.label: src/runtime auto-detecting abstractions
nodes.rationale: TCP sockets, worker threads, SQLite and HTTP serve live behind small abstractions that auto-detect at startup, so the same file runs unchanged under bun run, node and deno run.

nodes.label: Ask pattern (request/response)
nodes.rationale: tell is fire-and-forget; ref.ask<Reply>(msg) spawns a one-shot reply actor, wires it as both replyTo and context.sender, and resolves the promise when the target replies.

nodes.label: Event-sourced actor example
nodes.rationale: State is rebuilt from a journal on every restart, so there is no in-place mutation and no 'did this write commit?' question. The sample shows both style rules at once: onEvent is a fold that computes a value and stays inline, onCommand is a dispatch and every arm delegates.

nodes.label: Quick start
nodes.rationale: bun add / npm install / npm: specifier for Deno, then a Greeter actor in a dozen lines; the same file runs unchanged on all three runtimes.

nodes.label: Published comparison benchmark tables
nodes.rationale: One machine, one harness, a hundred interleaved rounds, every row verified against work the system actually completed rather than work it was asked for. Presented as ratios, not absolutes, over local in-process message paths only — nothing there says anything about clustering, persistence or a real network.

nodes.label: Chat and voice example applications
nodes.rationale: Two end-to-end sample apps, each with six interchangeable frontends talking the same WebSocket protocol to a clustered backend, exercising sharding, DistributedPubSub, PersistentActor, DistributedData, ClusterSingleton and failover.
